brief.headline: Push for maker-direct pricing — they are 100% a trader, so our price carries a reseller margin we can cut out

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match a manufacturer's price or introduce us directly to their maker
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to ₹0.65–0.80/pc for induction-wad caps at volume (the lower end of the market band ₹0.55–1.20/pc)
priceAsk.basis: They sell 100.0% traded goods — zero manufacturing — so every rupee we pay includes their mark-up. The open market shows ₹0.55–1.20/pc for a 28 mm PP cap, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. We should target that lower band or go direct to the maker.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — don't offer faster payment

brief.financialLeverage: They earn ₹54.69 Cr a year and keep only 2.8% as profit — very thin. We spend ₹65.27 L with them, which is 1.19% of everything they sell, so we matter. But their money-health score is just 2/10 and they sit in the grey zone (distress score 1.58), plus they have pending legal cases. That means we have buying power, but squeezing price too hard could break supply. The real win is cutting out the trading margin — either they drop to maker pricing or we source the maker ourselves.

evidence.point: They are purely a trader — they make nothing themselves
We are a significant customer to them
evidence.figure: Our ₹65.27 L is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Their money-health is weak and they are in the distress grey zone
They already stretch payment to their own suppliers far longer than peers
evidence.figure: They take 105d to pay suppliers vs 57d peer median

evidence.point: Open-market pricing for similar caps shows room to negotiate down at volume
evidence.figure: 28 mm PP cap: ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100) — makes pharma bottles and caps in-house, a strong second source

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-packaging leader (₹946.50 Cr, health B 73/100) — direct manufacturer for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — pan-India resin and packaging maker, medium confidence

risks: Weak money-health (2/10) and grey-zone distress (1.58) plus pending legal cases — supply continuity is a real risk; do not sole-source
Profit is only 2.8% — a hard price squeeze could tip them over; frame the ask around removing trading margin, not cutting into their operations
They are 100% a trader — we have no direct relationship with the actual maker, so if they fold or lose that maker, we have no fallback; qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek now
They take 105d to pay their own suppliers (vs 57d peer) — they are already stretched, so any supply hiccup from upstream will hit us fast
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but since you're trading these parts rather than making them, we'd like to talk about how we can work together to get closer to the manufacturer's price — or even meet the maker directly.
